title: A locally invertible module map is bijective on stalks of that open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $M,N$ sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\varphi:M\to N$ a module morphism, and $U\subseteq X$ an open subset. If $\varphi|_U$ is an isomorphism, then for every $x\in U$ the induced map of stalks $\varphi_x:M_x\to N_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is bijective.

source.place: Lemma AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.bijective_stalk_of_isIso_restrict, lines 464-485; its proof by the Mathlib natural isomorphism restrictStalkNatIso.

proof.text: Set y=(x,hx), a point of U. Mathlib Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso U.ι y naturally identifies the stalk functor after restriction with the original stalk functor at x. Naturality expresses the original stalk map as the inverse of the comparison at M, followed by the restricted stalk map, followed by the comparison at N.

The restricted map is an isomorphism by hypothesis, so its image under the underlying-presheaf and stalk functors is an isomorphism. The two comparison maps are isomorphisms as components of a natural isomorphism. Their composite is therefore an isomorphism of abelian groups, hence bijective by ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso. This is precisely the existing source lemma, whose sorry map entry has s=false and ts=false.
